findings.desc: Timeout stop reasons regress to provider_unhealthy for real host subprocess timeouts. main classified /timeout|timed out/ as AutopilotStopReason timeout before budget/validation fallback; this branch calls classifyAutopilotProviderFailure before the timeout branch in packages/main/src/core/lattice-autopilot.ts:1217-1220. The new classifier treats any "timeout"/"timed out" text as retryable network_unreachable in packages/main/src/core/autopilot-reliability.ts:95-96. Real Claude subprocess failures emit warning text "claude-code real subprocess timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms" from packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:2377-2386, and auto.status===failed builds the classification message from warnings plus nextAction in packages/main/src/core/lattice-autopilot.ts:1654-1658, so this existing timeout contract now becomes status paused_requires_resume with stopReason provider_unhealthy instead of failed/timeout. Read-only probe confirmed classifyAutopilotProviderFailure("timed out after 1000ms") returns network_unreachable/retryableProviderHealth=true.

Must-level B-320f verification evidence is semantically incomplete. CHK-002 adversarial requires invalid/zero maxConcurrentLive values to clamp to a safe minimum, but the cited smoke only constructs createAutopilotThrottleState(3) and exercises raise/backoff/hold; it never calls 0, negative, NaN, or Infinity even though the clamp lives in autopilot-reliability.ts. CHK-006 happy requires transient failures to produce waiting/paused autopilot_run states instead of generic failed status, but the new smoke only calls helper functions; existing autopilot-run/resume/migration smokes contain no provider_unhealthy/paused_requires_resume/waiting_for_provider_health assertion against autopilot_run. The planner sees 25 fresh evidence entries by hash, but these entries are partially vacuous for M2/M3 must intents.

docs/requirements/decisions/autopilot-v2-reliability-execution-plan.md:386 overclaims that retryable 429/503/529/overload/network/timeout become provider-health states. The implementation classifies dispatch timeout before provider-health classification (packages/main/src/core/lattice-autopilot.ts:1212-1220), so autopilot_run timeout remains stopReason=timeout/failed. The new regression smoke explicitly asserts that real-host timeout contract (packages/main/src/tasks/autopilot-run-smoke.ts:1100-1121), while provider transient overload separately pauses with stopReason=provider_unhealthy (packages/main/src/tasks/autopilot-run-smoke.ts:1123-1142). The dedicated reliability smoke covers provider health events but does not prove timeout becomes a provider-health state (packages/main/src/tasks/autopilot-v2-reliability-smoke.ts:15-70).

Provider-transient autopilot_run coverage is a false positive: autopilot-run-smoke passes host="http-503-overloaded", but lattice-dispatch only accepts fake/codex/claude-code/antigravity/gemini, so dispatch_auto throws an unknown-host validation error. classifyDispatchError then calls classifyAutopilotProviderFailure on that validation text, and the embedded host string matches 503/overloaded, producing provider_unhealthy/paused_requires_resume. This masks local validation errors as provider health and does not prove real provider transient failures still pause. Evidence: packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:453 rejects unknown hosts and packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:3239 throws the unknown-host error; packages/main/src/core/lattice-autopilot.ts:1212 routes non-timeout/non-validation text into provider classification; packages/main/src/tasks/autopilot-run-smoke.ts:1123 uses the invalid host string and asserts paused_requires_resume.
